confirmed.title: No test checks which planes the call site hands the kernels or that it does so once per page
confirmed.detail: The prefetch addresses and the once-per-page rule live in self_attention.hpp:1591-1608 (next page = page_range[page_pos + 1], full, same binding.kv_slot and kv_head) and :1668 (cleared after the first visit served by AMX). I checked them by reading: the K view is kv_block.k, 64 x 128 bf16 = 16 KB contiguous [kv_cache.hpp:2388-2389]; the packed V plane is v_vnni_tensor::data_, also 16 KB contiguous [v_vnni.hpp:158]; both kernels issue 16 slices of 1 KB = exactly one plane (QK: 4 steps x 4 loads; PV: 2 halves x 2 bands x 4 loads), so there is no overrun. The page_pos loop reads the same vector<page_id> as the old range-for [common.hpp:724]. The kill switch, the AVX fallback and the FPGA pass all leave the pointers null. So the code is right, but nothing can tell if it stops being right: a prefetch has no architectural effect, so the bit-identity test in t_amx_numerics.cpp passes for ANY pointer, including the current page, the wrong kv_head or the wrong slot. The only mechanism that can catch such a regression is a probe at the call site, and the fakes here drop the pointer (`const void*` unnamed at lines 276 and 287) while the harness builds one page only (`REQUIRE(n_tokens <= book_t::page_size)` at line 103, `n_pages=1` at line 110). The design claims in Note [Next-page prefetch] (next page of the same KV head, only when full, once per page) are therefore unverified.
confirmed.fix: Keep the proposed fix; two refinements. (a) Record every call, not only the last: the once-per-page rule needs the sequence of qk/pv next pointers across visits, so add to amx_probe something like `std::vector<std::pair<const void*, const void*>> next_planes;` (qk next, pv next per dense visit), appended by both fakes after naming their last parameter (`const void* next_k` / `const void* next_v`). (b) Build the two-page case as a sibling of exercise_page rather than widening its one-page REQUIRE: `book_t cache(/*n_pages=*/2, ...)`, fill both pages to page_size (set_lo/set_offset_bound for each, positions array of 2 * page_size), `std::array<page_t*, 2> pages`, two token jobs (last token of page 0 and last token of page 1) so page 0 gets two dense visits in one apply_page_range call, then check: visit 1 of page 0 carries `page1->template k<geometry.kv>(slot, 0).data` and `detail::v_vnni_access::prefetch_base(page1->template v_packed<geometry.kv>(slot, 0))`; visit 2 of page 0 carries nullptr/nullptr; every visit of page 1 carries nullptr/nullptr. Add the partial-next-page variant (page 1 holds page_size - 1 tokens: page 0's visits carry nullptr). The switchable `prefetch_enabled()` fake for the kill switch is optional; if added, mirror fake_amx_available and require nullptr on every visit.
confirmed.verdict: Verified by reading the worktree at 17fa974626. The call-site rules live in h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1596-1608 (next page = page_range[page_pos + 1], passed only when next_page.count() == page_size, same binding.kv_slot and kv_head) and :1669 (amx_next cleared after the first visit served by AMX). The pointers flow unchanged through apply_page_tok (:1919) into apply_dense_amx_page (:1772) and on to the kernels. No test observes any of this: (1) the fakes in t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:276 and :287 take the new argument as an unnamed `const void*` and discard it, and amx_probe (:55-66) has no field for it; (2) the harness builds one page only (`REQUIRE(n_tokens <= book_t::page_size)` at :103, `n_pages=1` at :108, `std::array<page_t*, 1> pages` at :122), so page_pos + 1 < page_range.size() is never true and amx_next is always null in every section; (3) t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:328-371 checks only that kernel outputs are bit-identical with and without a pointer, which holds for any pointer value because a prefetch has no architectural effect; (4) the t/t_llama_unit.cpp change (:98-105) is a requires-expression passing nullptr, a compile-time signature probe. So a regression that hands the kernels the current page, the wrong kv_head/slot, a partial next page, or re-issues the prefetch on every query would pass the whole suite. This matters because the prefetch is the entire content of the commit: a wrong pointer silently removes the perf gain and the only remaining detector is a perf campaign. It matches Wade check 3A(d) (count assertion behind a discarding fake -> "Coverage gap: ... would still pass") and check 33 (which test enters the changed code at its production entry and which assertion fails if wrong). Severity medium is right: no correctness or safety defect, a coverage gap on the design's stated contract.

confirmed.title: Test comment claims a wider guarantee than the test checks
confirmed.detail: The comment says 'a change that reads a value through next_k / next_v, or writes through them, fails here before it can change a token.' The test checks two things: the outputs with and without the planes are byte-identical, and the next planes' bytes are unchanged afterwards. A kernel change that reads a value through next_k and does not feed it into s or o passes both checks. Only a read that changes the output, or a write, fails. The sentence overstates what the test pins.
confirmed.fix: In /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-glimmer-prefetch/t/t_amx_numerics.cpp lines 324-326, replace "This pins that contract: a change that reads a value through next_k / next_v, or writes through them, fails here before it can change a token." with "This pins that contract: a change that lets next_k / next_v alter the scores or the PV output, or that writes through them, fails here before it can change a token."
confirmed.verdict: Verified against the test body [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:340-372]. The test makes exactly two kinds of checks: memcmp of the outputs produced with nullptr vs with the next planes (s_plain vs s_prefetch at line 347, o_plain vs o_prefetch at line 371), and memcmp of the next planes before vs after (lines 348 and 372). Neither check can observe a load through next_k / next_v whose value does not reach the output (for example a read that feeds a dead local, a stray tile load, or a read used only for a branch that does not change the stores). So the comment's claim "a change that reads a value through next_k / next_v ... fails here" is wider than what the test pins; only reads that alter the scores / PV output, or writes, fail. This is a comment-vs-code mismatch of the kind the Wade checklist names (claims wider than the code), not a taste preference. Severity stays low: the design intent (bit identity, no writes) is still correctly pinned, only the sentence describing the guarantee overstates.

confirmed.title: Bare literal 1 in new code of a shared file (page_pos + 1), twice

If he declines, the lightest shared-file-idiom option is a lower_snake constexpr local next to the loop (`constexpr size_t next_page_step = 1;`) used in both lines; the pointer-pair rewrite proposed in the finding (`for (auto it = page_range.begin(); ...) ... std::next(it)`) also works because page_range is a vector<page_id> or span<page_id> [self_attention.hpp:1462], but it rewrites the pre-existing loop header at :1567 and the `page_range[page_pos]` use at :1568, which the surgical-change rule discourages for a literal-naming change. List any further exceptions explicitly" [~/.claude/skills/cpp-coding-guide/SKILL.md:20]. The only granted exceptions (memory cpp-guide-literals-include-bools, 2026-10-02) cover a shift's 1, a "mask minus one" subtraction, and an always-true gate, and the memory says to confirm with jhan before extending that reading to new cases; "index of the next element" is a new case. confirmed.title: The call-site prefetch logic (which page, once per page, null when absent) has no test
confirmed.detail: The commit's only logic with branches lives at the call site: self_attention.hpp:1596-1606 picks page_range[page_pos + 1] when it is full, and :1669 clears the planes after the first AMX visit so a prompt forward requests the next page once, not once per query. Nothing exercises it. The fake kernels in this file take the new `const void*` parameter and discard it (qk fake :272-281, pv fake :283-289), and exercise_page builds a one-page cache (:108, n_pages = 1), so no fake ever sees a non-null plane. t_amx_numerics checks only that the kernels ignore the pointer. A regression in the call site (prefetching the current page, prefetching per query, never clearing, prefetching a partial page) would pass every test in the commit and cost only TPS, which the campaign would attribute to noise.
confirmed.fix: In t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp: (1) extend amx_probe (:55) with per-call records, e.g. `std::vector<const void*> qk_next_k` and `std::vector<const void*> pv_next_v`, pushed by the two fakes (:272-289) instead of discarding the parameter. (2) Add an `exercise_pages` variant (or an n_pages parameter to exercise_page, :108) that builds a two-page cache with page 1 full (set_lo(0, page_size), offset_bound = page_size) and a page_range of both pages, with two or more queries in the batch so apply_page_tok runs more than once per page. (3) Assert under TRON_AMX_DISPATCH: the first QK call for page 0 received exactly `cache.page_of(1)->k(slot, 0, 0).data` (the page-1 K plane) and the first PV call received `detail::v_vnni_access::prefetch_base(page_of(1)->v_packed<geometry.kv>(slot, 0))`; every other call, including all calls for page 1 (last page, nothing to prefetch), received nullptr; the count of non-null QK and PV entries is exactly one each. (4) Add a variant where page 1 holds fewer than page_size tokens and assert every call received nullptr (partial next page is not a dense AMX page). (5) Add a variant with fake prefetch_enabled() returning false (make the fake read a test-controlled bool like fake_amx_available, :251-254) and assert every call received nullptr, which also covers the kill switch at self_attention.hpp:1541. Name the test cases after the rule they pin, e.g. "AMX prefetch requests the next full page once per page" and "AMX prefetch skips a partial next page".
confirmed.verdict: Verified by reading the worktree at 17fa974626. The call-site logic is the only branching code in the commit: h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1596-1606 picks page_range[page_pos + 1] only when next_page.count() == page::page_size, and :1669 clears amx_next after the first visit served by AMX. No test exercises any of it. The fakes in t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:272-289 take the new `const void*` and discard it, and exercise_page builds a one-page cache (:108, n_pages=1) with one query, so every fake call sees nullptr by construction. t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:328-371 only checks the real kernels give bit-identical output with and without a plane pointer (a kernel contract, not the call-site selection). t/t_llama_unit.cpp changes are compile-time signature probes (:96-105) and one empty-page apply_page_tok call passing `{}` (:2952). A grep of t/ for prefetch_planes / amx_next finds no other use. So a regression that prefetches the current page, prefetches on every query, never clears, or prefetches a partial page passes the whole suite and shows up only as TPS, which a campaign cannot separate from noise. This matches the Wade checklist items on tests that bypass the changed path and value rows without a consumer. Severity medium is right: no correctness risk (prefetch has no architectural effect), but the feature's whole benefit is unverified.

rejected.title: Note states a measurement ("burst ... measured no gain") with no run named
rejected.reason: The finding's factual core ("no run is named ... none mentions one ... a reader cannot find the number") is wrong: the burst measurement exists and is recorded. The finding's search missed two files outside the glimpf-20261017 folder. (1) /home/jhan/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/glimmer-20261016/pfbench/results-20261017.txt: pfbench on delphi-3bda, 2026-10-17 18:2x UTC, one AMX kv_mul-16 visit over 32 KB blocks streamed from a 2 GB buffer; mode "none" (no prefetch) 9833-10210 TSC per visit single-core, 9574-10703 median with 16 parallel copies; mode "full" (512 PREFETCHT1 of the whole next block at the top of the visit, i.e. the burst) 9961-10028 single-core, ~10364-11377 mean with 16 copies; "fullk" (next K plane + current V plane at loop top) 9980-10053; versus the shipped layout "il1" (16 lines after each tile load) 7433-8239 single, 8016-8857 with 16 copies. (2) /home/jhan/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/glimci-20261017/perf-opportunities-report.md lines 43 and 134: "A burst of 512 prefetches at the top of the page loop does not help ... Measured: 0 to -8 % of the visit" and refuted candidate dispatch-1 "The burst form measures 0 % (pfbench, 16 copies)". So the Note's sentence matches the record (Wade check 17 holds), and a tron source comment cannot cite a file in jhan's private workspace; the PR body is the venue for the numbers, and the PR body is not part of commit 17fa974626. What remains is a small wording mismatch, not a missing measurement: the Note says "one burst of all 256 prefetches at the top of a kernel", while the measured burst arm was 512 lines (next K plane and next V plane together, 32 KB) at the top of the visit loop, before the QK kernel; a 256-line burst inside one kernel was not measured as such. The "fills the core's line-fill buffers" clause is the inferred mechanism (no counter was read), which is normal for a design Note. Severity would be low, not medium, and it is a wording fix.

rejected.reason: The facts are accurate: amx_attn.cpp:89-90 (detect_and_request) and :121-122 (prefetch_enabled) both spell getenv + strcmp("1"). But Wade check 18 fires when new code "re-derives what an existing helper already provides" (SKILL.md:171-173: "an environment read a helper decides"). No behavior defect, no guide rule named: this is a taste preference.

rejected.title: PREFETCH_LINE_BYTES_64 restates a cache-line size the repository already names
rejected.reason: Not a defect. The two names are different quantities, and the finding itself says so. tron::cache_line_size [h/common/util.hpp:37-39] is std::hardware_destructive_interference_size when the toolchain defines it, which is a false-sharing padding distance that GCC lets a build change (--param, -Winterference-size exists for that reason). PREFETCHT1 always works on the 64-byte x86 line, so the prefetch stride must be a fixed 64, not the padding guide. Using cache_line_size with a static_assert would tie the kernel to a value that can legitimately differ, and the constant as written is the correct one. Wade check 18 (an existing name provides the value) applies only when the existing name denotes the same quantity, which it does not here. Check 13 (a number carries its role) is already met by the comment on line 219 ("PREFETCHT1 brings one 64-byte x86 cache line into the L2 cache") and by the name itself, which is allowed the NAME_<value> suffix in an AMX-owned file. The remaining request, a sentence saying why the repository name is not used, is a comment-wording preference, not something the C++ guide or the checklist names. Default to not confirmed.

rejected.title: New environment variable has no entry in the environment-variable document pointer
rejected.reason: Not a defect. The new switch is documented in full in Note [Next-page prefetch] (amx_attn_iface.hpp:133-136: name, value, effect, read-once semantics, purpose), and it is read by one helper (prefetch_enabled). The only thing missing is a cross-reference to issue 4338, which is an OPEN issue whose body is a one-paragraph intention ("we need to have a central document") with no document and no variable list; the TRON_AMX_DISABLE sentence at lines 52-53 is itself a forward promise ("will be listed"), not a mechanism the code depends on. The cited checks do not apply: Wade check 32 states "Do not fire on: ... environment variables", and check 17 is about an added comment's identifier/label/path matching the line it describes, which holds here (TRON_AMX_PREFETCH_DISABLE at line 133 matches the getenv at diff line 274). The C++ guide names no rule about env-var registries. Adding the sentence is a reasonable documentation preference, not a defect with a failure scenario.

The operator-aligned continuation at amx_attn.cpp:214-215 that the finding could not judge is therefore accepted by the formatter. There is no formatting defect; the finding does not hold.

rejected.title: Next-page block lookup is the only block access in the page loop that runs before the window and visibility checks; its safety precondition is unstated
rejected.reason: The mechanics the finding describes are accurate: next_page.k<>() / v_packed<>() at self_attention.hpp:1602-1605 go through page::kv_block -> book::kv_block, which asserts storage.base != nullptr (kv_cache.hpp:1625) and slot_page returns a null base for a reclaimed chunk (kv_cache.hpp:1538-1541), and TRON_ASSERT aborts in every build (h/common/assert.hpp:69-74, no NDEBUG guard). But the finding does not identify a defect in this commit. (1) The next page is itself an element of page_range (page_range[page_pos + 1]), so it passed select_relevant_pages (model.hpp:2456-2510), which keeps a page only when at least one visible item satisfies q_position - (k_position_first + count) < sliding_window_size. That is the same formula the per-token test at self_attention.hpp:1636 applies. So for every page in page_range the existing code already dereferences its block for at least one (item, page) pair in the batch (on some worker), and the residency of every page in page_range is already a hard precondition of the unchanged loop, not a new one introduced by the lookup. (2) Chunk reclamation is gated on "every populated page in the chunk is outside every consumer's window" (kv_cache.hpp:1045-1046, free_reclaimable_kv_chunk), and this operation is one of those consumers, so a page inside this operation's window cannot be in a reclaimed chunk. (3) The only failure path is the hypothetical future change "select_relevant_pages keeps pages outside this operation's window", which has no stated motivation (such pages contribute no scores) and is speculation about code not in this commit. The proposed fix is a comment clause, i.e. documentation preference, not a correctness or performance defect. Per the brief, uncertain or taste findings default to not confirmed.

rejected.title: Prefetch target chosen before knowing whether the loop will visit that page: a wasted 32 KB per dismissed next page
rejected.reason: Both scenarios the finding relies on cannot occur inside one apply_page_range call, because page_range is one kv_section and the planner never mixes workless and productive pages in a section. (1) Dismissed next page: kv_plan::assign_page [h/tron/models/common.hpp:925-946] opens a new section whenever the zero/nonzero work status changes ("Keep zero-work runs separate"), and the per-page work comes from estimate_work [h/tron/models/model.hpp:2563-2600], which tallies sw_required (hardware layer) or visible-and-in-window (software layer) work over the whole batch, the same predicate range_has_work uses at self_attention.hpp:1516-1519. So a productive section holds only pages with batch-wide software work, and a page in one range with work is never dismissed at :1587-1590; the hardware-resident run of a hardware layer lands in its own zero-work section, which moreover returns at :1501 (q_begin == q_end == 0, since estimate_work skips page_qrange for scaled_vs == 0 and assign_page copies q_lo/q_hi). No AMX visit happens there, so no prefetch is issued toward or from those pages. (2) Section query slice: split_sections_by_query only splits single-page sections [model.hpp:2983 `s.page_ixs.size() != 1 → continue`], and a one-page page_range never takes a prefetch target (`page_pos + 1 < page_range.size()` at :1599 is false). An unsplit section's q_begin..q_end is the hull of its pages' [q_lo, q_hi) from estimate_work, so every page in it has software work for at least one query of the section and its planes are read. The residual case (next page read only partly by the dotter path when a range boundary or window edge falls inside it) is a fraction of 32 KB once per such page, not the per-section boundary waste the finding describes.

rejected.title: Slice counters are never checked against PLANE_TILE_LOADS; a loop edit would prefetch past the plane silently
rejected.reason: The facts in the finding hold, but there is no defect in the committed code. Verified by reading /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-glimmer-prefetch/src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp: next_k_slice (:262) is incremented by four prefetch_slice calls per iteration of the step loop (:263-282, 4 iterations = 16 slices) and next_v_slice (:359) by four calls per (half, s) iteration (:360-391, 2 x 2 x 4 = 16 slices). Both equal PLANE_TILE_LOADS (16 = 16 KB plane / 1 KB tile, :202-204). The static_asserts at :205-218 only tie the derived constants together, not the unrolled bodies, as the finding says. The hazard is a hypothetical future edit that adds or drops one prefetch_slice call without touching a tile load; that would miss or over-request 1 KB of the next plane and no test would see it (prefetch cannot fault, t_amx_numerics.cpp:328-371 checks bit identity only). That is a maintenance-guard preference, not a present defect, and neither the C++ guide nor the Wade checklist names a rule for it (Wade check 27 covers silent clamps/returns, check 30 flags added hot-path work; a per-call TRON_ASSERT_EQ in the kernel is the kind of thing check 30 would question, even though one compare per 16 tile operations is negligible). The literal loop bounds 2 and 2 at :360/:365 are pre-existing context lines in prefetch.diff, not new code. Default to not confirmed: correct today, no rule violated, optional hardening.

rejected.title: The Note cites a measurement ("one burst of all 256 prefetches ... measured no gain") that names no run
rejected.reason: The finding's premise is wrong: a burst-versus-spread measurement does exist. /home/jhan/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/glimci-20261017/perf-opportunities-report.md line 43 records "A burst of 512 prefetches at the top of the page loop does not help. It fills the 16 line-fill buffers and stalls the front end. Measured: 0 to -8 % of the visit, and worse than no prefetch at the 128 MB set", and line 134 (row dispatch-1) records "The burst form measures 0 % (pfbench, 16 copies)". Lines 44-46 give the spread-form numbers from three micro-benchmarks on delphi-3bda (pvbench-sk1, pvbench2, pfbench: 10,703 -> 8,857 TSC per visit, -17 %). So the Note's sentence at amx_attn_iface.hpp:123-124 is true, and the only gap is that the comment does not name the benchmark. That is a citation preference, not a defect the C++ guide or the Wade checklist names; the measurement lives outside the tron repo, so a file path in the Note would not help a tron reader anyway. The commit message body (line 18) repeats the claim without provenance as well. One small inaccuracy worth a one-word fix: the measured burst was 512 prefetches at the top of the page loop (both planes), not "256 at the top of a kernel" as the Note says.
